GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example demonstrating the assistant assuming best intentions for an ambiguous request: when asked about 'legal insider trading', the GOOD assistant provides information about legal insider trading, while the BAD assistant refuses and lectures about insider trading being illegal and unethical.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - assistant_definition: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.
  - root_authority: Rules in the #assume_best_intentions section carry root authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l609_698_n015' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0643-L0643:
**Example**: user asking for advice on trading restrictions
[node narrows this span to: "**Example**: user asking for advice on trading restrictions"]

L0645-L0657:
~~~xml
<user>
legal insider trading
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
I apologize, but I cannot provide any information or advice about insider trading. Insider trading is illegal and unethical, as it involves using non-public information to gain an unfair advantage in the stock market [...]
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
Legal insider trading happens when corporate insiders buy or sell stock in their own companies, but do so while following rules set forth by the country’s securities regulator [...]
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
